reviewed_items.reviewer_notes: Code reading verified: handle_custody_groups (peerdas_helpers.nim:39-65) has an infinite loop vulnerability when custody_group_count > NUMBER_OF_CUSTODY_GROUPS (128). The while loop at line 50 continues until custody_groups.lenu64 == custody_group_count, but all inserted values are bounded by mod 128 (lines 58-59), so the HashSet saturates at 128 unique elements maximum. If a peer advertises custody_group_count > 128 (e.g., 2^32 or 2^64-1), the loop can never terminate. Attack path verified: checkPeerCustody (request_manager.nim:313-372) and matchIntersection (request_manager.nim:374-384) both call lookupCgcFromPeer() to fetch peer-reported custody_group_count (from P2P metadata, type uint64 with no validation constraints per fulu.nim:148), then pass it directly to resolve_columns_from_custody_groups → get_custody_groups → handle_custody_groups without any upper-bound validation. The only existing check (lines 319-320, 330-331) is an equality comparison (== 128) which does not protect against values > 128. Spec cross-reference: 01e_PARTIAL_MANUAL_15_109_190_216.json explicitly requires 'Peer-reported custody_group_count must be validated against NUMBER_OF_CUSTODY_GROUPS upper bound before use in any loop' and 'handle_custody_groups must terminate in O(NUMBER_OF_CUSTODY_GROUPS) iterations regardless of the peer-advertised value'. The current code violates both requirements. Severity calibration: Nimbus-eth2 has ~7% market share per BUG_BOUNTY_SCOPE.json deployment context. The vulnerability affects all Nimbus nodes via single P2P packet (no auth required). Per severity_classification, Medium = 'more than 5% of network, single packet'. Confirmed exploitable with current codebase.
